units.title: Reasons and causes
units.summary: Ways to give a reason with extra nuance: emphasis ({からこそ}), guesswork ({せいか}), evidence ({ことから}), regret ({ばかりに}), excuses ({もん}), and expectations ({だけあって} / {だけに}).

points.title: 〜からこそ
points.meaning: precisely because; it is exactly because ... that
points.structure: Plain form + からこそ　／　Noun / な-adj + だからこそ
points.explanation:
{こそ} spotlights the word before it, so {からこそ} means "it is **this** reason, and no other, that explains the result." It is especially common when the reason might seem to point the opposite way: being strict because you care, resting because you are busy.

The sentence often ends with {のだ} / {んです}, which reinforces the explaining tone. {だからこそ} can also stand alone at the start of a sentence to mean "and that is exactly why...".

It works in both speech and writing, and you will hear it in speeches, interviews and advertising: {皆様[みなさま]の支[ささ]えがあったからこそ} ("it is only thanks to everyone's support").

examples.jp: 毎日[まいにち]練習[れんしゅう]したからこそ、優勝[ゆうしょう]できたのだと思[おも]う。
examples.en: I think it was precisely because we practised every day that we were able to win.

examples.jp: あなたのことを大切[たいせつ]に思[おも]っているからこそ、厳[きび]しく言[い]うんです。
examples.en: It's exactly because I care about you that I'm being strict.

examples.jp: 忙[いそが]しいからこそ、休[やす]みの日[ひ]はしっかり休[やす]むようにしている。
examples.en: It's precisely because I'm busy that I make sure to rest properly on my days off.

examples.jp: お客様[きゃくさま]の声[こえ]があったからこそ、この商品[しょうひん]は生[う]まれました。
examples.en: This product exists only because of our customers' feedback.

points.notes: {ので} cannot be followed by {こそ}; use {から}. {からこそ} is about emphasis, not about obligation; compare {からには} ("now that...") in the next unit.

quiz.q: 失敗[しっぱい]を経験[けいけん]した＿＿、人[ひと]の痛[いた]みがわかるようになった。
quiz.en: It's precisely because I've experienced failure that I came to understand other people's pain.

quiz.q: 君[きみ]を信頼[しんらい]している＿＿、この仕事[しごと]を任[まか]せるんだ。
quiz.en: It's exactly because I trust you that I'm leaving this job to you.

points.title: 〜せいか
points.meaning: perhaps because; maybe due to
points.structure: Plain form + せいか　／　Noun + のせいか　／　な-adj + なせいか
points.explanation:
{せい} names a cause that is blamed for a bad result. Adding the question particle {か} makes the cause a guess: "maybe it's because of X". The speaker is not certain, so {せいか} is a softer, more tentative way to explain something.

The result is usually negative or at least unwelcome (tiredness, headaches, an empty shop), though in casual speech it can also describe neutral changes.

A very common set phrase is {気[き]のせいか} "maybe it's just my imagination, but...".

examples.jp: 年[とし]のせいか、最近[さいきん]疲[つか]れやすくなった。
examples.en: Maybe it's my age, but I get tired easily these days.

examples.jp: 昨日[きのう]遅[おそ]くまで起[お]きていたせいか、頭[あたま]が痛[いた]い。
examples.en: Perhaps because I stayed up late last night, I have a headache.

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]のせいか、今日[きょう]は店[みせ]が空[す]いている。
examples.en: Maybe because of the rain, the shop is quiet today.

examples.jp: 気[き]のせいか、部長[ぶちょう]は今日[きょう]機嫌[きげん]が悪[わる]いようだ。
examples.en: Maybe it's just me, but the department head seems to be in a bad mood today.

points.notes: {せいで} states the cause as fact and blames it; {せいか} only guesses. For a good result use {おかげか} ("perhaps thanks to").

quiz.q: 寝不足[ねぶそく]の＿＿、今日[きょう]は仕事[しごと]に集中[しゅうちゅう]できない。
quiz.en: Maybe because I didn't get enough sleep, I can't concentrate on work today.

quiz.q: 気[き]の＿＿、彼[かれ]は少[すこ]し元気[げんき]がないように見[み]えた。
quiz.en: Maybe it was just my imagination, but he looked a bit down.

points.title: 〜ことから
points.meaning: from the fact that; because (as evidence or origin)
points.structure: Plain form + ことから　／　Noun + である + ことから　／　な-adj + な / である + ことから
points.explanation:
{ことから} points to a fact and says that a judgment, conclusion or name comes from it. Think of it as "judging from the fact that..." or "since...".

Two uses are especially common:
- **Evidence**: police or reporters explaining a conclusion ({〜ことから、警察[けいさつ]は〜とみている}).
- **Origin of a name**: {〜ことから、〜と呼[よ]ばれている} ("it is called ... because ...").

It is formal and written in tone, so you will meet it constantly in news articles, signs at tourist sites and explanations, less in everyday chat.

examples.jp: 道[みち]が濡[ぬ]れていることから、夜中[よなか]に雨[あめ]が降[ふ]ったとわかった。
examples.en: From the fact that the road was wet, I could tell it had rained during the night.

examples.jp: この橋[はし]は形[かたち]が眼鏡[めがね]に似[に]ていることから、「眼鏡橋[めがねばし]」と呼[よ]ばれている。
examples.en: This bridge is called the "Spectacles Bridge" because its shape resembles a pair of glasses.

examples.jp: 現場[げんば]に足跡[あしあと]が残[のこ]っていたことから、警察[けいさつ]は犯人[はんにん]が複数[ふくすう]いるとみている。
examples.en: Because footprints were left at the scene, police believe there was more than one culprit.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]から近[ちか]く家賃[やちん]も安[やす]いことから、この地域[ちいき]は学生[がくせい]に人気[にんき]がある。
examples.en: Since it is close to the station and rents are cheap, this area is popular with students.

quiz.q: 部屋[へや]の電気[でんき]がついている＿＿、誰[だれ]かいると思[おも]われる。
quiz.en: Since the lights in the room are on, it seems someone is there.

quiz.q: この坂[さか]は桜[さくら]の木[き]が多[おお]い＿＿、「桜坂[さくらざか]」と呼[よ]ばれている。
quiz.en: This slope is called "Sakura-zaka" because it has many cherry trees.

points.title: 〜ばかりに
points.meaning: just because; simply because (with a bad result)
points.structure: Plain form + ばかりに　／　Noun + である + ばかりに　／　V-たい + ばかりに
points.explanation:
{ばかりに} says that one (often small) cause led to a bad outcome, and it carries a strong feeling of regret: "if only that hadn't happened...". The result is always something unfortunate.

A special pattern is {〜たいばかりに}, "purely out of the desire to...". Here the person does something extreme or costly because they want something so badly.

It appears in both speech and writing, typically when telling a story about a mistake.

examples.jp: 一言[ひとこと]余計[よけい]なことを言[い]ったばかりに、彼女[かのじょ]を怒[おこ]らせてしまった。
examples.en: Just because I said one unnecessary thing, I made her angry.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]が道[みち]を間違[まちが]えたばかりに、みんなが電車[でんしゃ]に乗[の]り遅[おく]れた。
examples.en: Simply because I took the wrong road, everyone missed the train.

examples.jp: パスワードを忘[わす]れたばかりに、手続[てつづ]きに一時間[いちじかん]もかかった。
examples.en: All because I forgot my password, the procedure took a whole hour.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもに会[あ]いたいばかりに、彼[かれ]は毎週[まいしゅう]五百[ごひゃく]キロも運転[うんてん]した。
examples.en: Purely out of wanting to see his children, he drove 500 km every week.

points.notes: Do not use {ばかりに} for good results; use {おかげで}. It is not the same as {〜たばかり} ("have just done").

quiz.q: 確認[かくにん]を怠[おこた]った＿＿、大[おお]きなミスにつながってしまった。
quiz.en: Just because I neglected to double-check, it led to a big mistake.

quiz.q: 合格[ごうかく]し＿＿ばかりに、彼[かれ]は寝[ね]る時間[じかん]も削[けず]って勉強[べんきょう]した。
quiz.en: Purely out of wanting to pass, he studied even at the expense of sleep.

points.title: 〜もの / 〜もん（ものだから）
points.meaning: because, you see (personal excuse or justification)
points.structure: Plain form + もの / もん（だもん・んだもん）　／　Plain form + ものだから / もんだから / ものですから
points.explanation:
At the end of a sentence, {もの} (casual {もん}) gives a personal reason, often as a self-justifying excuse: "but I'm tired!" It usually comes with {だって} at the start and often in the form {〜んだもん}. The tone is childish or sweet, typical of children, young people and close friends.

In the middle of a sentence, {ものだから} / {もんだから} explains a reason for something the speaker feels was unavoidable. The polite {ものですから} is often used when apologising: "the train stopped, you see, so...".

Both stress that the speaker feels the reason excuses them.

examples.jp: 「どうして食[た]べないの？」「だって、まずいんだもん。」
examples.en: "Why aren't you eating?" "Because it tastes bad!"

examples.jp: 行[い]きたくないよ。疲[つか]れてるもん。
examples.en: I don't want to go. I'm tired.

examples.jp: 道[みち]が混[こ]んでいたものですから、遅[おく]れてしまいました。申[もう]し訳[わけ]ありません。
examples.en: The roads were congested, you see, so I'm late. I'm very sorry.

examples.jp: あまりにかわいかったもんだから、つい買[か]っちゃった。
examples.en: It was just so cute that I ended up buying it.

points.notes: Never use sentence-final {もん} to a boss or customer. At work, {ものですから} is acceptable, but apologise first so it doesn't sound like you are only making excuses.

quiz.q: 「なんで泣[な]いてるの？」「だって、ママが怒[おこ]った＿＿。」
quiz.en: "Why are you crying?" "Because Mum got angry!"

quiz.q: 電車[でんしゃ]が止[と]まってしまった＿＿、会議[かいぎ]に間[ま]に合[あ]いませんでした。
quiz.en: The train stopped, you see, so I didn't make it to the meeting.

points.title: 〜だけあって
points.meaning: as you would expect from; living up to (praise)
points.structure: Plain form + だけあって　／　Noun / な-adj stem + だけあって
points.explanation:
{だけあって} says that a result matches what you would expect, given someone's status, effort or reputation. It is almost always used to **praise**: the five-star hotel really does have great service; the person who lived abroad really does speak naturally.

It often appears with {さすが} at the start: {さすが〜だけあって}. A similar, slightly more formal variant is {〜だけのことはある} at the end of a sentence ("...is worth its reputation").

Because it is evaluative, the second half is a positive comment, not an action or request.

examples.jp: さすが一流[いちりゅう]ホテルだけあって、サービスが素晴[すば]らしい。
examples.en: As you'd expect of a top-class hotel, the service is excellent.

examples.jp: 十年[じゅうねん]もアメリカに住[す]んでいただけあって、彼[かれ]の英語[えいご]は自然[しぜん]だ。
examples.en: As you'd expect from someone who lived in America for ten years, his English is natural.

examples.jp: 毎日[まいにち]練習[れんしゅう]しているだけあって、ピアノがとても上手[じょうず]だ。
examples.en: Since she practises every day, it's no surprise she plays the piano very well.

examples.jp: 人気店[にんきてん]だけあって、平日[へいじつ]でも行列[ぎょうれつ]ができている。
examples.en: It's a popular restaurant, so it's no wonder there's a queue even on a weekday.

points.notes: Opposite expectation: {にしては} / {わりに} ("for a ..., surprisingly"). See {だけに} for the difference between the two.

quiz.q: プロの料理人[りょうりにん]＿＿、味付[あじつ]けが完璧[かんぺき]だ。
quiz.en: As you'd expect from a professional chef, the seasoning is perfect.

quiz.q: 高[たか]かった＿＿、このコートはとても暖[あたた]かい。
quiz.en: As you'd expect given how expensive it was, this coat is very warm.

points.title: 〜だけに
points.meaning: all the more because; precisely because (good or bad)
points.structure: Plain form + だけに　／　Noun / な-adj stem + だけに
points.explanation:
{だけに} also links a situation to a natural consequence, but it adds the idea of "all the more". Because of X, the feeling or result is stronger than usual.

The key difference from {だけあって}:
- {だけあって} is praise: the result lives up to expectations.
- {だけに} can be positive **or negative**, and is very common with emotions like disappointment or shock: {期待[きたい]していただけに、がっかりした} ("I was looking forward to it, so I was all the more disappointed").

It also describes natural characteristics: {年末[ねんまつ]だけに混[こ]んでいる} ("it's the end of the year, so of course it's crowded").

examples.jp: 期待[きたい]していただけに、試合[しあい]に負[ま]けたときはショックだった。
examples.en: I'd had such high hopes, so losing the match was all the more of a shock.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は若[わか]いだけに、新[あたら]しいことを覚[おぼ]えるのが速[はや]い。
examples.en: Being young, he is quick to pick up new things.

examples.jp: 年末[ねんまつ]だけに、駅[えき]はどこも人[ひと]でいっぱいだ。
examples.en: It being the end of the year, every station is packed with people.

examples.jp: 一生懸命[いっしょうけんめい]準備[じゅんび]しただけに、中止[ちゅうし]になって本当[ほんとう]に残念[ざんねん]だ。
examples.en: Because we prepared so hard, it's all the more disappointing that it was cancelled.

points.notes: Quick test: if the result is bad or is an emotion such as {残念[ざんねん]}, {ショック} or {悔[くや]しい}, choose {だけに}. If it is praise that matches a reputation, both may work, but {だけあって} is the typical choice.

quiz.q: 楽[たの]しみにしていた＿＿、コンサートが中止[ちゅうし]になって本当[ほんとう]にがっかりした。
quiz.en: I'd been looking forward to it, so I was all the more disappointed when the concert was cancelled.

quiz.q: 相手[あいて]は小[ちい]さい子[こ]ども＿＿、少[すこ]しも目[め]が離[はな]せない。
quiz.en: Since I'm dealing with a small child, I can't take my eyes off them for a second.

units.title: Now that..., just because..., unless...
units.summary: Premises that lead to a decision ({からには}, {以上[いじょう]}, {うえは}), premises that don't guarantee a result ({からといって}), and conditions with negatives ({ないことには}, {ないことはない}).

points.title: 〜からには
points.meaning: now that; since (I've done X, I must / will)
points.structure: Plain form + からには　／　Noun + である + からには
points.explanation:
{からには} takes a fact or decision ("now that I've accepted the job", "since we're entering the race") and says what naturally follows from it. The second half expresses the speaker's **resolve, duty, wish or advice**: {〜つもりだ}, {〜たい}, {〜なければならない}, {〜べきだ}, {〜よう}.

The idea is "having come this far, I should go all the way". It is common in speech and in fairly formal writing alike.

The first half is usually a past action (the {た} form) or a firm plan (dictionary form).

examples.jp: 約束[やくそく]したからには、守[まも]らなければならない。
examples.en: Now that I've promised, I have to keep it.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に来[き]たからには、日本語[にほんご]が話[はな]せるようになりたい。
examples.en: Since I've come to Japan, I want to become able to speak Japanese.

examples.jp: 試合[しあい]に出[で]るからには、優勝[ゆうしょう]を目指[めざ]そう。
examples.en: If we're going to compete, let's aim to win.

examples.jp: 引[ひ]き受[う]けたからには、最後[さいご]まで責任[せきにん]を持[も]ってやります。
examples.en: Now that I've taken it on, I'll see it through responsibly to the end.

points.notes: The second half must be a judgment or intention, not a simple description. ✗ {日本[にほん]に来[き]たからには、雨[あめ]が多[おお]い}.

quiz.q: 社長[しゃちょう]に任[まか]された＿＿、絶対[ぜったい]にこのプロジェクトを成功[せいこう]させたい。
quiz.en: Now that the president has entrusted it to me, I absolutely want to make this project succeed.

quiz.q: 留学[りゅうがく]する＿＿、現地[げんち]の友達[ともだち]をたくさん作[つく]るつもりだ。
quiz.en: Since I'm going to study abroad, I intend to make lots of local friends.

points.title: 〜以上[いじょう]（は）
points.meaning: since; as long as; given that
points.structure: Plain form + 以上[いじょう]（は）　／　Noun + である + 以上[いじょう]（は）
points.explanation:
Outside of numbers, {以上[いじょう]} works like {からには}: given this fact, a certain conclusion, duty or decision follows. The tone is more **objective and logical**, so it is common in rules, contracts, business and formal arguments.

Unlike {からには}, it sits comfortably with a negative premise used as a logical basis: {証拠[しょうこ]がない以上[いじょう]} ("as long as there is no evidence"). Adding {は} gives slightly more emphasis.

The second half is a conclusion such as {〜べきだ}, {〜しかない}, {〜わけにはいかない}, {〜てもらいます}.

examples.jp: 学生[がくせい]である以上[いじょう]、勉強[べんきょう]が第一[だいいち]だ。
examples.en: As long as you're a student, studying comes first.

examples.jp: 契約[けいやく]を結[むす]んだ以上[いじょう]、期限[きげん]は守[まも]っていただきます。
examples.en: Since you have signed the contract, we will ask you to meet the deadline.

examples.jp: 引[ひ]き受[う]けた以上[いじょう]は、途中[とちゅう]でやめるわけにはいかない。
examples.en: Having taken it on, I can't just quit halfway.

examples.jp: 証拠[しょうこ]がない以上[いじょう]、彼[かれ]を犯人[はんにん]と決[き]めつけることはできない。
examples.en: As long as there is no evidence, we can't conclude that he is the culprit.

points.notes: Rough formality scale for "now that": {からには} (neutral, personal resolve) → {以上[いじょう]は} (logical, formal) → {うえは} (stiff, written).

quiz.q: プロである＿＿、言[い]い訳[わけ]は許[ゆる]されない。
quiz.en: As long as you're a professional, excuses aren't acceptable.

quiz.q: 規則[きそく]で決[き]まっている＿＿、従[したが]うしかない。
quiz.en: Given that it's set by the rules, we have no choice but to follow it.

points.title: 〜うえは（上[うえ]は）
points.meaning: now that (formal); having reached this point
points.structure: V-plain (usually た-form) + うえは / 上[うえ]は
points.explanation:
{うえは} is the stiffest member of the "now that" family. It follows a serious event or decision and leads to a firm resolution: "now that things have come to this, I will...".

You will see it in formal writing, official statements, speeches, novels and period dramas, rarely in casual talk. The set phrase {こうなったうえは} ("now that it has come to this") is the most common use.

The second half expresses strong resolve or obligation: {〜しかない}, {〜べきだ}, {〜つもりだ}, or a command.

examples.jp: こうなったうえは、自分[じぶん]の力[ちから]でやるしかない。
examples.en: Now that it's come to this, I have no choice but to do it on my own.

examples.jp: 決心[けっしん]した上[うえ]は、もう迷[まよ]わない。
examples.en: Now that I've made up my mind, I won't hesitate any more.

examples.jp: 計画[けいかく]が決定[けってい]した上[うえ]は、全員[ぜんいん]で協力[きょうりょく]して進[すす]めてください。
examples.en: Now that the plan has been decided, please all work together to carry it out.

examples.jp: 事故[じこ]の原因[げんいん]が明[あき]らかになった上[うえ]は、会社[かいしゃ]として責任[せきにん]を取[と]るべきだ。
examples.en: Now that the cause of the accident is clear, the company should take responsibility.

points.notes: Don't mix up the {上[うえ]} patterns: {上[うえ]は} = now that; {上[うえ]で} = after doing / in the process of; {上[うえ]に} = on top of, in addition to.

quiz.q: こうなった＿＿、覚悟[かくご]を決[き]めて戦[たたか]うしかない。
quiz.en: Now that it's come to this, I have no choice but to steel myself and fight.

quiz.q: 試験[しけん]を受[う]けると決[き]めた＿＿、全力[ぜんりょく]で準備[じゅんび]する。
quiz.en: Now that I've decided to take the exam, I'll prepare with everything I've got.

points.title: 〜からといって
points.meaning: just because ... (doesn't mean)
points.structure: Plain form + からといって　／　Noun / な-adj + だからといって
points.explanation:
{からといって} quotes a reason someone might use and then rejects the conclusion: "just because X, it doesn't follow that Y". The second half is almost always negative:
- {〜わけではない} (it's not that...)
- {〜とは限[かぎ]らない} (it's not necessarily...)
- {〜てはいけない} / {〜のはよくない} (you shouldn't...)

In casual speech it shortens to {からって}. {だからといって} can also start a sentence: "Even so, that doesn't mean...".

examples.jp: 安[やす]いからといって、必要[ひつよう]のない物[もの]を買[か]うのはやめよう。
examples.en: Just because something is cheap, let's not buy things we don't need.

examples.jp: 体[からだ]にいいからといって、そればかり食[た]べてはいけない。
examples.en: Just because it's good for you doesn't mean you should eat nothing else.

examples.jp: 日本人[にほんじん]だからといって、敬語[けいご]が完璧[かんぺき]に使[つか]えるわけではない。
examples.en: Just because someone is Japanese doesn't mean they can use keigo perfectly.

examples.jp: 給料[きゅうりょう]が高[たか]いからといって、いい会社[かいしゃ]とは限[かぎ]らない。
examples.en: A high salary doesn't necessarily mean it's a good company.

examples.jp: 謝[あやま]ったからって、すぐ許[ゆる]してもらえるとは思[おも]わないほうがいい。
examples.en: Don't assume you'll be forgiven right away just because you apologised.

quiz.q: 有名[ゆうめい]な大学[だいがく]を出[で]た＿＿、仕事[しごと]ができるとは限[かぎ]らない。
quiz.en: Just because someone graduated from a famous university doesn't necessarily mean they're good at their job.

quiz.q: 暑[あつ]い＿＿、一日中[いちにちじゅう]エアコンの前[まえ]にいるのはよくない。
quiz.en: Just because it's hot, it's not good to stay in front of the air conditioner all day.

points.title: 〜ないことには
points.meaning: unless; if ... not, then (can't)
points.structure: V-ない + ことには　／　い-adj くない + ことには　／　Noun / な-adj + でないことには
points.explanation:
{ないことには} sets up a necessary condition: unless X happens, Y can't happen. The second half is negative or describes an impossible or difficult situation: {〜できない}, {〜わからない}, {〜始[はじ]まらない}.

It is a stronger, more emphatic version of {〜なければ〜ない}. It appears in both speech and writing, and is very common at work when you need information or approval before you can act.

examples.jp: 食[た]べてみないことには、おいしいかどうか判断[はんだん]できない。
examples.en: Unless I try it, I can't judge whether it's good.

examples.jp: 実際[じっさい]に会[あ]ってみないことには、どんな人[ひと]かわからない。
examples.en: You can't tell what someone is like until you actually meet them.

examples.jp: 予算[よさん]が決[き]まらないことには、計画[けいかく]を進[すす]められない。
examples.en: Unless the budget is settled, we can't move the plan forward.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]の許可[きょか]がないことには、契約[けいやく]はできません。
examples.en: Without the president's approval, we can't sign the contract.

points.notes: The second half must be negative. ✗ {勉強[べんきょう]しないことには、合格[ごうかく]できる}.

quiz.q: 現場[げんば]を見[み]＿＿、正確[せいかく]な見積[みつ]もりは出[だ]せません。
quiz.en: Unless I see the site, I can't give you an accurate estimate.

quiz.q: 本人[ほんにん]に聞[き]いてみないことには、＿＿。
quiz.en: Unless we ask the person directly, we won't know the real reason.
choices: 本当[ほんとう]の理由[りゆう]はわからない

points.title: 〜ないことはない（ないこともない）
points.meaning: it's not that ... not; it's possible, but
points.structure: V-ない / い-adj くない / Noun・な-adj じゃない + ことはない（こともない）
points.explanation:
A double negative that gives a **weak, reluctant yes**: "it's not that I can't..." or "I suppose it's possible, but...". It is often followed by {けど} / {が} and a reservation.

Use it when you don't want to say a flat "no" but also don't want to commit, which makes it very useful in Japanese social and work situations.

{〜ないこともない} is a slightly softer variant. Both are common in conversation.

examples.jp: 急[いそ]げば間[ま]に合[あ]わないことはない。
examples.en: If we hurry, it's not impossible to make it in time.

examples.jp: 「納豆[なっとう]、食[た]べられる？」「食[た]べられないことはないけど、あまり好[す]きじゃない。」
examples.en: "Can you eat natto?" "It's not that I can't, but I don't really like it."

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の気持[きも]ちもわからないこともない。
examples.en: I can sort of understand how he feels.

examples.jp: 明日[あした]までに仕上[しあ]げられないことはありませんが、品質[ひんしつ]は保証[ほしょう]できません。
examples.en: It's not impossible to finish it by tomorrow, but I can't guarantee the quality.

points.notes: Compare {〜ことはない} after a dictionary form, which means "there's no need to": {心配[しんぱい]することはない} ("no need to worry").

quiz.q: タクシーで行[い]けば、間[ま]に合[あ]わ＿＿。
quiz.en: If we go by taxi, it's not impossible to make it in time.

quiz.q: 「お酒[さけ]、飲[の]めますか。」「飲[の]めない＿＿が、あまり強[つよ]くないです。」
quiz.en: "Do you drink?" "It's not that I can't, but I'm not much of a drinker."

units.title: Possibility, risk, and difficulty
units.summary: Verb-stem endings that say whether something can happen ({得[う]る}), might go wrong ({おそれがある}, {かねない}), is hard to accept ({がたい}), is politely refused ({かねる}), or is simply impossible ({っこない}).

points.title: 〜得[う]る / 〜得[え]ない
points.meaning: can (possibly) happen / cannot possibly
points.structure: V-ます stem + 得[う]る（得[え]る）／ 得[え]ない
points.explanation:
{得[う]る} means "to be possible" in the sense of **likelihood**, not personal skill. {起[お]こり得[う]る} = "could happen", {考[かんが]え得[う]る} = "conceivable". The negative {得[え]ない} means "cannot possibly".

The dictionary form can be read {うる} or {える}; {うる} sounds more formal and written. All other forms use {え}: {得[え]ます}, {得[え]ない}, {得[え]た}.

The most frequent word by far is {あり得[う]る} / {あり得[え]ない}. In casual speech, young people use {ありえない！} to mean "No way! / Unbelievable!".

examples.jp: それは十分[じゅうぶん]あり得[う]る話[はなし]だ。
examples.en: That's an entirely plausible story.

examples.jp: 大[おお]きな地震[じしん]は、いつでも起[お]こり得[う]る。
examples.en: A major earthquake could happen at any time.

examples.jp: 考[かんが]え得[う]る限[かぎ]りの方法[ほうほう]を試[ため]した。
examples.en: We tried every method we could think of.

examples.jp: この問題[もんだい]は、一社[いっしゃ]だけでは解決[かいけつ]し得[え]ない。
examples.en: This problem cannot be solved by one company alone.

points.notes: Not for ability: ✗ {私[わたし]は泳[およ]ぎ得[う]る}. Use {泳[およ]げる} for "I can swim".

quiz.q: このような事故[じこ]は、どの工場[こうじょう]でも起[お]こり＿＿。
quiz.en: An accident like this could happen at any factory.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]が嘘[うそ]をつくなんて、あり＿＿。
quiz.en: There's no way she would lie.

points.title: 〜おそれがある
points.meaning: there is a risk / danger that
points.structure: V-dictionary + おそれがある　／　Noun + のおそれがある
points.explanation:
{おそれ} (written {恐[おそ]れ} or {虞[おそれ]}) means "fear, danger". {〜おそれがある} warns that something **bad** might happen. It is objective and formal, so it is the standard expression in weather reports, safety warnings, medicine labels and news.

It is never used for good possibilities. For a neutral "might", use {〜かもしれない} or {〜可能性[かのうせい]がある}.

The polite form {〜おそれがあります} is standard in announcements. Earthquake bulletins use a related phrase for the opposite case: {津波[つなみ]の心配[しんぱい]はありません} ("there is no danger of a tsunami").

examples.jp: 台風[たいふう]の影響[えいきょう]で、明日[あした]は大雨[おおあめ]になるおそれがあります。
examples.en: Due to the typhoon, there is a risk of heavy rain tomorrow.

examples.jp: この薬[くすり]は眠[ねむ]くなるおそれがあるので、運転[うんてん]の前[まえ]には飲[の]まないでください。
examples.en: This medicine may cause drowsiness, so do not take it before driving.

examples.jp: 津波[つなみ]のおそれがあるため、海岸[かいがん]から離[はな]れてください。
examples.en: Because of the risk of a tsunami, please move away from the coast.

examples.jp: このままでは、顧客[こきゃく]の情報[じょうほう]が外部[がいぶ]に漏[も]れるおそれがある。
examples.en: If things continue like this, customer information could leak outside the company.

quiz.q: 大雨[おおあめ]により、今夜[こんや]川[かわ]が氾濫[はんらん]する＿＿があります。
quiz.en: Due to the heavy rain, there is a risk the river will flood tonight.

quiz.q: この製品[せいひん]は、使[つか]い方[かた]によっては火災[かさい]につながる＿＿があります。
quiz.en: Depending on how it is used, this product could cause a fire.

points.title: 〜かねない
points.meaning: might well (do something bad); could end up
points.structure: V-ます stem + かねない
points.explanation:
Despite the {ない}, {かねない} is **not** negative in meaning. It says "there's a real chance this bad thing will happen". It reflects the speaker's own worry or criticism, so it is more subjective than {おそれがある}.

Typical uses: warning someone ({事故[じこ]を起[お]こしかねない}), pointing out risks at work ({問題[もんだい]になりかねない}), or saying a person is capable of doing something bad ({あの人[ひと]なら言[い]いかねない}).

It is used in both speech and writing; the polite form is {かねません}.

examples.jp: そんな運転[うんてん]をしていたら、事故[じこ]を起[お]こしかねないよ。
examples.en: If you drive like that, you could well cause an accident.

examples.jp: 睡眠不足[すいみんぶそく]が続[つづ]くと、体[からだ]を壊[こわ]しかねません。
examples.en: If your lack of sleep continues, you may end up ruining your health.

examples.jp: 小[ちい]さなミスが、大[おお]きな問題[もんだい]につながりかねない。
examples.en: A small mistake could lead to a big problem.

examples.jp: あの人[ひと]なら、そのくらいのことは言[い]いかねない。
examples.en: He's just the kind of person who might say something like that.

points.notes: {おそれがある}: objective warning (news, labels). {かねない}: the speaker's own concern. Neither is used for good outcomes.

quiz.q: このままでは、締[し]め切[き]りに間[ま]に合[あ]わなくなり＿＿。
quiz.en: At this rate, we could end up missing the deadline.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]の不用意[ふようい]な発言[はつげん]は、誤解[ごかい]を招[まね]き＿＿。
quiz.en: His careless remark could well cause misunderstandings.

points.title: 〜かねる
points.meaning: cannot (politely); be unable to bring oneself to
points.structure: V-ます stem + かねる / かねます
points.explanation:
{かねる} means "I find it hard to / I'm not in a position to". In practice it is a **polite refusal**, and it is everywhere in Japanese customer service and business:
- {わかりかねます} "I'm afraid I can't say"
- {お答[こた]えしかねます} "I'm unable to answer"
- {いたしかねます} "We are unable to do that"

It sounds softer than {できません} because it suggests the speaker would like to help but can't. Outside of business it can express personal reluctance: {賛成[さんせい]しかねる} ("I can't quite agree").

Don't confuse it with {かねない} ("might well"), which looks negative but isn't.

examples.jp: 申[もう]し訳[わけ]ございませんが、そのご質問[しつもん]にはお答[こた]えしかねます。
examples.en: I'm very sorry, but I'm unable to answer that question.

examples.jp: 個人情報[こじんじょうほう]に関[かん]することは、お教[おし]えいたしかねます。
examples.en: We are unable to disclose anything relating to personal information.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]の一存[いちぞん]では決[き]めかねますので、上司[じょうし]に確認[かくにん]いたします。
examples.en: I can't decide that on my own, so I'll check with my manager.

examples.jp: 正直[しょうじき]に言[い]うと、彼[かれ]の意見[いけん]には賛成[さんせい]しかねる。
examples.en: To be honest, I can't quite agree with his opinion.

examples.jp: 困[こま]っている様子[ようす]を見[み]るに見[み]かねて、手伝[てつだ]うことにした。
examples.en: I couldn't bear to just stand by and watch them struggle, so I decided to help.

points.notes: Remember: {かねる} = can't (polite refusal); {かねない} = might (bad thing). The idiom {見[み]るに見[み]かねて} means "unable to stand by and watch".

quiz.q: 申[もう]し訳[わけ]ございませんが、返品[へんぴん]はお受[う]けいたし＿＿。
quiz.en: We're very sorry, but we are unable to accept returns.

quiz.q: その件[けん]については、私[わたし]には判断[はんだん]し＿＿ので、担当者[たんとうしゃ]におつなぎします。
quiz.en: I'm not able to make a judgment on that matter, so I'll put you through to the person in charge.

points.title: 〜がたい
points.meaning: hard to (accept, believe, forgive...)
points.structure: V-ます stem + がたい
points.explanation:
{がたい} (from {難[かた]い}, "difficult") means that something is hard to do because of **inner resistance**: you can't bring yourself to believe it, forgive it or forget it. Common combinations: {信[しん]じがたい}, {許[ゆる]しがたい}, {理解[りかい]しがたい}, {忘[わす]れがたい}, {耐[た]えがたい}, {得[え]がたい} (precious, hard to come by).

It is formal and somewhat literary. You will see it in news commentary, essays and speeches.

For **physical or practical** difficulty, use {〜にくい} instead: {この靴[くつ]は歩[ある]きにくい}.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]がそんなことをしたとは、信[しん]じがたい。
examples.en: It's hard to believe that he did such a thing.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもを狙[ねら]った犯罪[はんざい]は、許[ゆる]しがたい。
examples.en: Crimes targeting children are unforgivable.

examples.jp: 留学中[りゅうがくちゅう]の一年[いちねん]は、忘[わす]れがたい思[おも]い出[で]になった。
examples.en: My year studying abroad became an unforgettable memory.

examples.jp: あのチームで働[はたら]けたことは、得[え]がたい経験[けいけん]だった。
examples.en: Being able to work on that team was an invaluable experience.

points.notes: {にくい} = hard for practical reasons (the pen is hard to write with). {がたい} = hard to accept emotionally or morally. {ありがたい} ("grateful") originally meant "rare, hard to exist".

quiz.q: 毎日[まいにち]一緒[いっしょ]に働[はたら]いていた彼[かれ]が会社[かいしゃ]のお金[かね]を盗[ぬす]んだなんて、信[しん]じ＿＿。
quiz.en: It's hard to believe that he, who worked with us every day, stole company money.

quiz.q: この靴[くつ]は重[おも]くて歩[ある]き＿＿。
quiz.en: These shoes are heavy and hard to walk in.

points.title: 〜っこない
points.meaning: no way; there's no chance that
points.structure: V-ます stem + っこない
points.explanation:
{っこない} is a strong, casual denial: "there's no way that will happen". Common combinations are {できっこない}, {わかりっこない}, {勝[か]てっこない}, {間[ま]に合[あ]いっこない}, {ばれっこない}.

It is **spoken and informal**, used with friends and family. In writing or polite speech, use {〜はずがない}, {〜わけがない} or {〜得[え]ない} instead.

It attaches to the verb stem, so it is {わかりっこない}, not ✗ {わからっこない}.

examples.jp: こんな難[むずか]しい問題[もんだい]、子[こ]どもにわかりっこないよ。
examples.en: There's no way a kid could understand a problem this hard.

examples.jp: 一日[いちにち]で全部[ぜんぶ]覚[おぼ]えるなんて、できっこない。
examples.en: Memorising all of it in one day? No way.

examples.jp: 黙[だま]っていれば、ばれっこないよ。
examples.en: If you keep quiet, there's no way anyone will find out.

examples.jp: あのチームに勝[か]てっこないってみんな言[い]うけど、やってみなきゃわからない。
examples.en: Everyone says there's no way we can beat that team, but you never know until you try.

quiz.q: 宝[たから]くじなんて、当[あ]たり＿＿よ。
quiz.en: There's no way you'll win the lottery.

quiz.q: 三十分[さんじゅっぷん]でレポートを書[か]くなんて、＿＿。
quiz.en: Write a report in thirty minutes? There's no way I can do that.

units.title: Strong feelings and how things look
units.summary: Expressing feelings you can't control ({てしょうがない}, {てたまらない}, {てならない}, {ずにはいられない}), exclamations ({ことか}), strong impressions ({ものがある}), and how someone appears ({げ}, {気味[ぎみ]}).

points.title: 〜てしょうがない / 〜て仕方[しかた]がない
points.meaning: so ... I can't stand it; extremely
points.structure: V-て / い-adj くて / な-adj で + しょうがない（仕方[しかた]がない・仕方[しかた]ない）
points.explanation:
Literally "there is no way (to deal with it)", this pattern says a feeling or sensation is so strong the speaker can't control it. It is the **most casual and most flexible** of the three "unbearably" patterns in this unit.

It works with emotions ({うれしくて}), physical sensations ({痛[いた]くて}), desires ({〜たくて}) and also with things that just keep bothering you ({気[き]になってしょうがない}, {眠[ねむ]くてしょうがない}).

{しょうがない} is the spoken form of {仕方[しかた]がない}. Normally it describes the speaker's own feelings; for other people add {〜ようだ} or {〜らしい}.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]が気[き]になってしょうがない。
examples.en: I can't stop worrying about my exam results.

examples.jp: 昨日[きのう]から歯[は]が痛[いた]くてしょうがない。
examples.en: My tooth has been killing me since yesterday.

examples.jp: 来週[らいしゅう]の旅行[りょこう]が楽[たの]しみでしょうがない。
examples.en: I'm so excited about next week's trip I can hardly stand it.

examples.jp: うちの子犬[こいぬ]がかわいくて仕方[しかた]がない。
examples.en: Our puppy is just unbearably cute.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {〜てもしょうがない} ("there's no point in..."): {今[いま]さら悔[く]やんでもしょうがない} = "there's no use regretting it now".

quiz.q: 冷房[れいぼう]が壊[こわ]れて、暑[あつ]く＿＿。
quiz.en: The air conditioner broke and it's unbearably hot.

quiz.q: 何度[なんど]も同[おな]じミスをする自分[じぶん]が情[なさ]けなく＿＿。
quiz.en: I feel so pathetic for making the same mistake again and again.
choices: ても仕方[しかた]がない

points.title: 〜てたまらない
points.meaning: unbearably; dying to
points.structure: V-て / い-adj くて / な-adj で + たまらない
points.explanation:
{たまらない} comes from {堪[たま]る} ("to endure"), so the pattern means "so ... that I can't endure it". It expresses an intense, often physical or emotional state: loneliness, joy, thirst, itchiness, a desire to see someone.

Compared with {てしょうがない}, it focuses more strongly on the **intensity of a feeling or bodily sensation**, and is slightly less casual. It is less natural with neutral states like {気[き]になる}.

It is very common with {〜たくてたまらない} ("dying to...").

examples.jp: 喉[のど]が渇[かわ]いてたまらない。
examples.en: I'm desperately thirsty.

examples.jp: 合格[ごうかく]の知[し]らせを聞[き]いて、うれしくてたまらなかった。
examples.en: When I heard I'd passed, I was overjoyed.

examples.jp: 一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしを始[はじ]めたばかりの頃[ころ]は、寂[さび]しくてたまらなかった。
examples.en: When I'd just started living alone, I was unbearably lonely.

examples.jp: 早[はや]く国[くに]の家族[かぞく]に会[あ]いたくてたまらない。
examples.en: I'm dying to see my family back home.

points.notes: {たまらない} on its own can also mean "irresistible": {この香[かお]り、たまらない！} ("This smell is amazing!").

quiz.q: 一日中[いちにちじゅう]何[なに]も食[た]べていないので、おなかがすいて＿＿。
quiz.en: I haven't eaten anything all day, so I'm starving.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]に会[あ]い＿＿たまらない。
quiz.en: I'm dying to see her.

points.title: 〜てならない
points.meaning: can't help feeling; terribly (spontaneous feeling)
points.structure: V-て / い-adj くて / な-adj で + ならない
points.explanation:
{てならない} describes a feeling that **wells up by itself** and won't go away. It is more formal and written than the other two patterns, and it is used mainly with:
- verbs of spontaneous perception: {気[き]がしてならない}, {思[おも]えてならない}, {感[かん]じられてならない}
- emotional adjectives: {心配[しんぱい]でならない}, {残念[ざんねん]でならない}, {不安[ふあん]でならない}

It is **not** normally used for physical sensations such as hunger or heat; use {てたまらない} or {てしょうがない} for those.

Summary of the three:
- {しょうがない}: casual, widest range
- {たまらない}: intense emotions and bodily sensations
- {ならない}: written, spontaneous feelings and impressions

examples.jp: 将来[しょうらい]のことが心配[しんぱい]でならない。
examples.en: I'm terribly worried about the future.

examples.jp: 何[なに]か大切[たいせつ]なことを忘[わす]れているような気[き]がしてならない。
examples.en: I can't shake the feeling that I've forgotten something important.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]が嘘[うそ]をついているように思[おも]えてならない。
examples.en: I can't help thinking that he's lying.

examples.jp: 恩師[おんし]が亡[な]くなったと聞[き]き、残念[ざんねん]でならない。
examples.en: I heard that my old teacher has passed away, and I am deeply saddened.

points.notes: Different from {〜てはならない} ("must not"): {嘘[うそ]をついてはならない} = "you must not lie".

quiz.q: あの日[ひ]、もっと早[はや]く連絡[れんらく]していれば助[たす]けられたような気[き]がして＿＿。
quiz.en: I can't shake the feeling that I could have helped if I'd contacted them sooner that day.

quiz.q: 事故[じこ]で亡[な]くなった方々[かたがた]のことを思[おも]うと、残念[ざんねん]＿＿。
quiz.en: When I think of the people who died in the accident, I feel deep regret.

points.title: 〜ずにはいられない
points.meaning: can't help doing; can't stop oneself from
points.structure: V-ない stem + ずにはいられない（する → せずにはいられない）
points.explanation:
{ず} is the classical form of {ない}, so this means "can't stay without doing": the speaker is compelled to act or react, often against their will. Common verbs: {笑[わら]う}, {泣[な]く}, {言[い]う}, {考[かんが]える}, {感[かん]じる}.

The spoken variant {〜ないではいられない} has the same meaning. Both are mainly used for the speaker's own reactions.

Irregular form: {する} becomes {せず}: {感動[かんどう]せずにはいられない}.

examples.jp: その映画[えいが]のラストシーンでは、泣[な]かずにはいられなかった。
examples.en: I couldn't help crying at the final scene of that film.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の話[はなし]があまりにおかしくて、笑[わら]わずにはいられなかった。
examples.en: His story was so funny I couldn't stop myself from laughing.

examples.jp: 困[こま]っている人[ひと]を見[み]ると、声[こえ]をかけずにはいられない。
examples.en: When I see someone in trouble, I can't help speaking to them.

examples.jp: 新[あたら]しいゲームが出[で]ると、買[か]わないではいられない。
examples.en: Whenever a new game comes out, I just have to buy it.

examples.jp: この記事[きじ]を読[よ]むと、政府[せいふ]の対応[たいおう]に疑問[ぎもん]を感[かん]じずにはいられない。
examples.en: Reading this article, one can't help questioning the government's response.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {〜ずにすむ} ("get away without doing") or {〜ざるを得[え]ない} ("have no choice but to", an outside obligation rather than an inner impulse).

quiz.q: あまりに理不尽[りふじん]な話[はなし]で、抗議[こうぎ]せ＿＿。
quiz.en: It was so unreasonable that I couldn't help protesting.
choices: ずにはいられなかった

quiz.q: 人[ひと]が困[こま]っているのを見[み]ると、助[たす]け＿＿いられない。
quiz.en: When I see someone in trouble, I can't help but help them.

points.title: 〜ことか
points.meaning: how (much) ...!; so very
points.structure: どんなに / どれほど / 何度[なんど] ... + Plain form + ことか　（な-adj: な / である）
points.explanation:
{ことか} turns a statement into an emotional exclamation about degree: "how happy I was!", "how long I waited!". It usually pairs with a question word of degree: {どんなに}, {どれほど}, {どれだけ}, {何度[なんど]}, {何回[なんかい]}.

It sounds heartfelt and a little literary, so you will find it in letters, speeches, essays and dramatic dialogue. In casual talk people would more often say {すごく〜た}.

Don't confuse it with {ものか}, which is a strong denial ("as if I would!").

examples.jp: 合格[ごうかく]の知[し]らせを聞[き]いて、どんなにうれしかったことか。
examples.en: How happy I was to hear I'd passed!

examples.jp: 君[きみ]からの連絡[れんらく]を、どれほど待[ま]っていたことか。
examples.en: You have no idea how long I waited to hear from you.

examples.jp: この仕事[しごと]を辞[や]めたいと思[おも]ったことが、何度[なんど]あったことか。
examples.en: I can't count how many times I've wanted to quit this job.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に来[き]たばかりの頃[ころ]、同僚[どうりょう]の親切[しんせつ]にどれだけ助[たす]けられたことか。
examples.en: When I'd just arrived in Japan, my colleagues' kindness helped me more than I can say.

quiz.q: 一人[ひとり]で外国[がいこく]に住[す]み始[はじ]めた頃[ころ]は、どんなに心細[こころぼそ]かった＿＿。
quiz.en: When I first started living abroad alone, how lonely and uneasy I felt!

quiz.q: あなたが無事[ぶじ]だと聞[き]いて、＿＿安心[あんしん]したことか。
quiz.en: You can't imagine how relieved I was to hear you were safe.

points.title: 〜ものがある
points.meaning: there is something (moving / impressive / hard) about it
points.structure: Plain form (V / い-adj / な-adj な) + ものがある
points.explanation:
{ものがある} expresses the speaker's strong impression that something has a certain quality, without pointing to one exact feature: "there's something touching about it", "it is pretty tough".

It often combines with verbs of emotion or evaluation: {心[こころ]を打[う]つものがある}, {胸[むね]に迫[せま]るものがある}, {光[ひか]るものがある} (shows promise), {驚[おどろ]くべきものがある}, or with adjectives like {つらい}, {厳[きび]しい}.

It is used in reviews, commentary and thoughtful conversation. It sounds measured and adult.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の演奏[えんそう]には、人[ひと]の心[こころ]を動[うご]かすものがある。
examples.en: There's something about his playing that moves people.

examples.jp: 毎日[まいにち]満員電車[まんいんでんしゃ]で通勤[つうきん]するのは、つらいものがある。
examples.en: Commuting on a packed train every day is pretty rough.

examples.jp: この町[まち]の変化[へんか]の速[はや]さには、驚[おどろ]くべきものがある。
examples.en: The speed at which this town is changing is quite astonishing.

examples.jp: 新人[しんじん]ながら、彼女[かのじょ]の企画力[きかくりょく]には光[ひか]るものがある。
examples.en: Although she's new, her planning skills really stand out.

quiz.q: この写真[しゃしん]には、見[み]る人[ひと]の胸[むね]に迫[せま]る＿＿がある。
quiz.en: There's something about this photo that deeply moves the viewer.

quiz.q: 四十代[よんじゅうだい]で一[いち]から転職[てんしょく]するのは、正直[しょうじき]厳[きび]しい＿＿。
quiz.en: Honestly, changing careers from scratch in your forties is pretty tough.

points.title: 〜げ
points.meaning: -looking; seeming (from someone's appearance)
points.structure: い-adj stem / な-adj stem / V-たい stem + げ（な / に / だ）
points.explanation:
{げ} describes how a feeling or state **shows on the outside**: {悲[かな]しげな顔[かお]} (a sad-looking face), {楽[たの]しげに笑[わら]う} (laugh happily). It behaves like a {な}-adjective.

It is mostly literary or written and is used for other people's visible emotions. Common words: {寂[さび]しげ}, {楽[たの]しげ}, {不安[ふあん]げ}, {得意[とくい]げ}, {意味[いみ]ありげ} (meaningful-looking), {言[い]いたげ} (looking as if wanting to say something).

In modern slang {よさげ} ("looks good") is common online.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもたちが公園[こうえん]で楽[たの]しげに遊[あそ]んでいる。
examples.en: The children are playing happily in the park.

examples.jp: 少女[しょうじょ]は寂[さび]しげな目[め]で窓[まど]の外[そと]を見[み]ていた。
examples.en: The girl was gazing out the window with lonely eyes.

examples.jp: 面接[めんせつ]を待[ま]つ学生[がくせい]たちは、みんな不安[ふあん]げだった。
examples.en: The students waiting for their interviews all looked anxious.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は何[なに]か言[い]いたげな顔[かお]をしていたが、結局[けっきょく]何[なに]も言[い]わなかった。
examples.en: He looked as if he wanted to say something, but in the end he said nothing.

points.notes: {そう} is the everyday equivalent and also predicts events ({雨[あめ]が降[ふ]りそう}). {げ} cannot predict events: ✗ {雨[あめ]が降[ふ]りげ}.

quiz.q: 母[はは]は駅[えき]で、寂[さび]し＿＿に手[て]を振[ふ]っていた。
quiz.en: At the station, my mother waved with a lonely look.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]は何[なに]か言[い]いた＿＿な様子[ようす]だった。
quiz.en: She looked as though she wanted to say something.

points.title: 〜気味[ぎみ]
points.meaning: a touch of; slightly; tending toward (something negative)
points.structure: V-ます stem / Noun + 気味[ぎみ]（だ / の）
points.explanation:
{気味[ぎみ]} says that a person or thing is **slightly** in some (usually undesirable) state right now: a touch of a cold, a bit tired, running a little behind. It softens the statement, which makes it very useful at work: {少[すこ]し遅[おく]れ気味[ぎみ]です} sounds less alarming than {遅[おく]れています}.

Common combinations: {風邪[かぜ]気味[ぎみ]}, {疲[つか]れ気味[ぎみ]}, {太[ふと]り気味[ぎみ]}, {遅[おく]れ気味[ぎみ]}, {緊張[きんちょう]気味[ぎみ]}, {不足[ふそく]気味[ぎみ]}.

It works as a noun: {気味[ぎみ]だ}, {気味[ぎみ]の}, {気味[ぎみ]で}.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は少[すこ]し風邪[かぜ]気味[ぎみ]なので、早[はや]めに帰[かえ]ります。
examples.en: I've got a touch of a cold today, so I'll head home early.

examples.jp: 最近[さいきん]、仕事[しごと]が忙[いそが]しくて疲[つか]れ気味[ぎみ]だ。
examples.en: Work has been busy lately and I'm a bit worn out.

examples.jp: 初[はじ]めてのプレゼンで、彼[かれ]は少[すこ]し緊張[きんちょう]気味[ぎみ]だった。
examples.en: It was his first presentation, and he seemed a little nervous.

examples.jp: 工事[こうじ]の進[すす]み具合[ぐあい]がやや遅[おく]れ気味[ぎみ]です。
examples.en: Construction is running slightly behind schedule.

points.notes: {気味[ぎみ]} = a slight degree of a state now ({風邪[かぜ]気味[ぎみ]}). {がち} = something tends to happen often ({休[やす]みがち}, often absent). {っぽい} = has the feel of ({子[こ]どもっぽい}).

quiz.q: 寝不足[ねぶそく]が続[つづ]いて、ちょっと疲[つか]れ＿＿だ。
quiz.en: I haven't been sleeping enough, so I'm a bit tired.

quiz.q: 作業[さぎょう]が予定[よてい]より遅[おく]れ＿＿なので、来週[らいしゅう]から人[ひと]を増[ふ]やします。
quiz.en: The work is running a little behind schedule, so we'll add more people from next week.

units.title: Time, occasions, and turning points
units.summary: Formal ways to talk about when things happen: ever since ({て以来[いらい]}), only after ({てはじめて}), as soon as ({次第[しだい]}), after careful steps ({上[うえ]で}), on occasions ({際[さい]に}, {にあたって}, {に先立[さきだ]って}), and triggers ({をきっかけに}).

points.title: 〜て以来[いらい]
points.meaning: ever since
points.structure: V-て + 以来[いらい]　／　Noun + 以来[いらい]
points.explanation:
{て以来[いらい]} marks a starting point in the past, and the second half describes a state or habit that has **continued ever since**: "since I came to Japan, I've kept a diary". The second half is therefore usually {〜ている}, a negative like {一度[いちど]も〜ていない}, or a long-term change.

It is not used for a single event that happened right after, or for the very recent past. ✗ {昨日[きのう]以来[いらい]} sounds odd; say {昨日[きのう]から}.

It works in speech and writing, and nouns such as {入社[にゅうしゃ]以来[いらい]}, {震災[しんさい]以来[いらい]} are common in news.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に来[き]て以来[いらい]、毎日[まいにち]日記[にっき]をつけている。
examples.en: Ever since I came to Japan, I've kept a diary every day.

examples.jp: 卒業[そつぎょう]して以来[いらい]、彼[かれ]とは一度[いちど]も会[あ]っていない。
examples.en: I haven't seen him once since we graduated.

examples.jp: 入社[にゅうしゃ]以来[いらい]、一日[いちにち]も休[やす]んだことがない。
examples.en: Since joining the company, I haven't taken a single day off.

examples.jp: 震災[しんさい]以来[いらい]、防災[ぼうさい]グッズを準備[じゅんび]する家庭[かてい]が増[ふ]えた。
examples.en: Since the earthquake disaster, more households have been preparing emergency supplies.

quiz.q: 大学[だいがく]を卒業[そつぎょう]して＿＿、ずっと東京[とうきょう]で働[はたら]いている。
quiz.en: Ever since graduating from university, I've been working in Tokyo.

quiz.q: その事故[じこ]＿＿、彼[かれ]は車[くるま]を運転[うんてん]しなくなった。
quiz.en: Since that accident, he has stopped driving.

points.title: 〜てはじめて（て初[はじ]めて）
points.meaning: only after; not until
points.structure: V-て + はじめて
points.explanation:
{てはじめて} says that a realisation or change came **only after** an experience: "only when I got sick did I understand how precious health is". The second half is typically a verb of realising: {わかる}, {気[き]づく}, {知[し]る}, {〜ようになる}.

It carries a reflective tone, as if the speaker is saying "I should have known earlier". It is common in essays, speeches and conversation alike.

It is often combined with {〜てみて}: {やってみてはじめて} ("not until I actually tried it").

examples.jp: 病気[びょうき]になってはじめて、健康[けんこう]のありがたさがわかった。
examples.en: Only after I got sick did I appreciate the value of good health.

examples.jp: 一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしをしてはじめて、親[おや]の苦労[くろう]を知[し]った。
examples.en: It wasn't until I lived alone that I understood how hard my parents worked.

examples.jp: 実際[じっさい]に働[はたら]いてみてはじめて、この仕事[しごと]の大変[たいへん]さに気[き]づいた。
examples.en: Only once I actually started working did I realise how demanding this job is.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に住[す]んではじめて、ごみの分別[ぶんべつ]がこんなに細[こま]かいと知[し]った。
examples.en: Not until I lived in Japan did I learn how detailed rubbish sorting is.

quiz.q: 海外[かいがい]に出[で]て＿＿、自分[じぶん]の国[くに]のよさがわかった。
quiz.en: Only after going abroad did I see the good points of my own country.

quiz.q: 失[うしな]って＿＿、その大切[たいせつ]さに気[き]づくものだ。
quiz.en: It's only after you lose something that you realise how important it was.

points.title: 〜次第[しだい]（as soon as）
points.meaning: as soon as
points.structure: V-ます stem + 次第[しだい]　／　Noun (する verbs) + 次第[しだい]
points.explanation:
{次第[しだい]} after a verb stem means "as soon as X happens, (I will) do Y". It is a polite, efficient expression used constantly in **business**: {分[わ]かり次第[しだい]ご連絡[れんらく]します} ("I'll contact you as soon as I know").

The second half must be a future action, intention or request by a person. You cannot use it for past events or for things that just happen naturally. ✗ {駅[えき]に着[つ]き次第[しだい]、雨[あめ]が降[ふ]った}.

The casual equivalent is {〜たらすぐ}. For {次第[しだい]で} ("depending on"), see Unit 13.

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]がやみ次第[しだい]、出発[しゅっぱつ]しましょう。
examples.en: Let's set off as soon as the rain stops.

examples.jp: 準備[じゅんび]ができ次第[しだい]、会議[かいぎ]を始[はじ]めてください。
examples.en: Please start the meeting as soon as everything is ready.

examples.jp: 詳細[しょうさい]が決[き]まり次第[しだい]、ご連絡[れんらく]いたします。
examples.en: We will contact you as soon as the details are decided.

examples.jp: 商品[しょうひん]が入荷[にゅうか]し次第[しだい]、発送[はっそう]いたします。
examples.en: We will ship the item as soon as it arrives in stock.

quiz.q: 結果[けっか]が分[わ]かり＿＿、メールでお知[し]らせします。
quiz.en: We'll let you know by email as soon as we have the results.

quiz.q: 田中[たなか]が戻[もど]り次第[しだい]、＿＿。
quiz.en: (On the phone to a client) As soon as Tanaka is back, I'll have him call you back.
choices: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]り出[だ]しました
会議[かいぎ]が終[お]わっていました
折[お]り返[かえ]しお電話[でんわ]させます
私[わたし]は帰[かえ]りました

points.title: 〜上[うえ]で
points.meaning: after (doing carefully); in doing / for the purpose of
points.structure: V-た + 上[うえ]で　／　Noun + の上[うえ]（で）　／　V-dictionary + 上[うえ]で
points.explanation:
{上[うえ]で} has two main uses.

**1. After the {た} form or a noun + {の}: "after doing X (and based on it)"**. X is a necessary first step before the main action: think it over, consult, confirm. It is more formal and deliberate than {〜てから}. Forms like {ご確認[かくにん]の上[うえ]} are standard on forms and in emails.

**2. After V-dictionary: "in doing / when it comes to"**. It introduces an area in which something is important or a problem: {日本[にほん]で生活[せいかつ]する上[うえ]で大切[たいせつ]なこと} ("what's important in living in Japan").

Both are common in business and formal speech.

examples.jp: よく考[かんが]えた上[うえ]で、お返事[へんじ]します。
examples.en: I'll give you my answer after thinking it over carefully.

examples.jp: 家族[かぞく]と相談[そうだん]した上[うえ]で決[き]めたいと思[おも]います。
examples.en: I'd like to decide after talking it over with my family.

examples.jp: 契約書[けいやくしょ]の内容[ないよう]をご確認[かくにん]の上[うえ]、ご署名[しょめい]ください。
examples.en: Please sign after confirming the contents of the contract.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]で生活[せいかつ]する上[うえ]で、在留[ざいりゅう]カードは欠[か]かせない。
examples.en: When it comes to living in Japan, your residence card is indispensable.

examples.jp: 外国語[がいこくご]を学[まな]ぶ上[うえ]で大切[たいせつ]なのは、毎日[まいにち]続[つづ]けることだ。
examples.en: What matters most in learning a foreign language is keeping at it every day.

quiz.q: 両親[りょうしん]とよく話[はな]し合[あ]った＿＿、留学[りゅうがく]を決[き]めた。
quiz.en: I decided to study abroad after discussing it thoroughly with my parents.

quiz.q: 仕事[しごと]をする＿＿、報告[ほうこく]・連絡[れんらく]・相談[そうだん]は欠[か]かせない。
quiz.en: In doing your job, reporting, keeping people informed and consulting are essential.

points.title: 〜際[さい]に（際[さい]は）
points.meaning: when; on the occasion of (formal)
points.structure: V-dictionary / V-た + 際[さい]（に / は）　／　Noun + の際[さい]（に / は）
points.explanation:
{際[さい]} is a formal word for "time, occasion", so {〜際[さい]に} is a stiffer version of {〜時[とき]に}. You will see it on signs, in announcements, manuals, official letters and business emails: {お降[お]りの際[さい]は足元[あしもと]にご注意[ちゅうい]ください}.

**{際[さい]} vs {時[とき]}**
- {時[とき]} is general: any time, any register, including states and periods ({子[こ]どもの時[とき]}, {暇[ひま]な時[とき]}).
- {際[さい]} refers to a **specific occasion or procedure**, usually a deliberate action, and sounds formal. It is not used for long states or ages: ✗ {子[こ]どもの際[さい]}.

In casual conversation, {際[さい]} would sound oddly stiff.

examples.jp: お降[お]りの際[さい]は、足元[あしもと]にご注意[ちゅうい]ください。
examples.en: Please watch your step when getting off.

examples.jp: 退室[たいしつ]する際[さい]には、必[かなら]ず電気[でんき]を消[け]してください。
examples.en: When leaving the room, please be sure to turn off the lights.

examples.jp: 緊急[きんきゅう]の際[さい]は、こちらの番号[ばんごう]にお電話[でんわ]ください。
examples.en: In case of emergency, please call this number.

examples.jp: 先日[せんじつ]京都[きょうと]へ出張[しゅっちょう]した際[さい]に、昔[むかし]の同僚[どうりょう]に会[あ]った。
examples.en: When I was on a business trip to Kyoto the other day, I met a former colleague.

quiz.q: 子[こ]どもの＿＿、よく川[かわ]で泳[およ]いだ。
quiz.en: When I was a child, I often swam in the river.

quiz.q: パスポートを申請[しんせい]する＿＿は、写真[しゃしん]が一枚[いちまい]必要[ひつよう]です。
quiz.en: When applying for a passport, you need one photo.

points.title: 〜にあたって（にあたり）
points.meaning: on the occasion of; when undertaking (something important)
points.structure: Noun / V-dictionary + にあたって・にあたり・にあたっては
points.explanation:
{にあたって} is used when facing an **important, one-time milestone**: starting a business, opening a ceremony, moving abroad, graduating. The second half usually describes preparations, attitude or a formal greeting.

{にあたり} is the more formal written version, typical of speeches: {開会[かいかい]にあたり、一言[ひとこと]ご挨拶[あいさつ]申[もう]し上[あ]げます}.

**vs {際[さい]に}**: {際[さい]} can be used for routine actions ({お降[お]りの際[さい]}), but {にあたって} is only for significant occasions. ✗ {トイレを使[つか]うにあたって}.

examples.jp: 新[あたら]しい生活[せいかつ]を始[はじ]めるにあたって、家具[かぐ]をそろえた。
examples.en: In preparation for starting my new life, I got all the furniture together.

examples.jp: 開会[かいかい]にあたり、一言[ひとこと]ご挨拶[あいさつ]申[もう]し上[あ]げます。
examples.en: On the occasion of this opening, allow me to say a few words.

examples.jp: 海外[かいがい]に進出[しんしゅつ]するにあたって、現地[げんち]の法律[ほうりつ]を詳[くわ]しく調[しら]べた。
examples.en: Before expanding overseas, we researched local laws in detail.

examples.jp: 本[ほん]サービスのご利用[りよう]にあたっては、利用規約[りようきやく]をお読[よ]みください。
examples.en: Before using this service, please read the terms of use.

quiz.q: 新[あら]たな事業[じぎょう]を始[はじ]める＿＿、社員[しゃいん]全員[ぜんいん]の意見[いけん]を聞[き]いた。
quiz.en: In starting the new business, we asked all employees for their opinions.

quiz.q: 卒業[そつぎょう]＿＿、お世話[せわ]になった先生方[せんせいがた]に心[こころ]からお礼[れい]を申[もう]し上[あ]げます。
quiz.en: On the occasion of our graduation, we sincerely thank the teachers who looked after us.

points.title: 〜に先立[さきだ]って（に先立[さきだ]ち）
points.meaning: prior to; ahead of
points.structure: Noun / V-dictionary + に先立[さきだ]って・に先立[さきだ]ち・に先立[さきだ]つ + Noun
points.explanation:
{先立[さきだ]つ} means "to go before". {〜に先立[さきだ]って} says something is done **before** a main event, usually as preparation or a preview: a press conference before a launch, an opening ceremony before a match.

It is formal and common in news reports and official announcements. {に先立[さきだ]ち} is even more formal, and {〜に先立[さきだ]つ + Noun} modifies a noun ({公開[こうかい]に先立[さきだ]つ試写会[ししゃかい]}).

In everyday speech, {〜の前[まえ]に} is the normal choice.

examples.jp: 試合[しあい]に先立[さきだ]って、開会式[かいかいしき]が行[おこな]われた。
examples.en: An opening ceremony was held prior to the match.

examples.jp: 新製品[しんせいひん]の発売[はつばい]に先立[さきだ]ち、記者会見[きしゃかいけん]が開[ひら]かれた。
examples.en: A press conference was held ahead of the new product's release.

examples.jp: 工事[こうじ]を始[はじ]めるに先立[さきだ]って、近所[きんじょ]の住民[じゅうみん]に説明会[せつめいかい]を行[おこな]った。
examples.en: Before starting construction, they held an information session for local residents.

examples.jp: 映画[えいが]の一般[いっぱん]公開[こうかい]に先立[さきだ]つ試写会[ししゃかい]に招待[しょうたい]された。
examples.en: I was invited to a preview screening held before the film's general release.

quiz.q: 首脳会談[しゅのうかいだん]に＿＿、両国[りょうこく]の外相[がいしょう]が会談[かいだん]した。
quiz.en: Ahead of the summit, the foreign ministers of both countries held talks.

quiz.q: 本格的[ほんかくてき]な販売[はんばい]＿＿、一部[いちぶ]の店舗[てんぽ]で試験的[しけんてき]に販売[はんばい]を行[おこな]う。
quiz.en: Prior to the full launch, trial sales will be held at some stores.

points.title: 〜をきっかけに（がきっかけで）
points.meaning: with X as the trigger; prompted by
points.structure: Noun / V-た + の + をきっかけに（して）・がきっかけで　／　（formal）を契機[けいき]に
points.explanation:
{きっかけ} is a trigger or chance that starts something new. {Xをきっかけに} means "X prompted (a new habit, interest or change)". Note the particles: {をきっかけに} or {がきっかけで}; don't mix them (✗ {がきっかけに}).

Typical topics are life changes: starting a hobby, changing jobs, moving, getting interested in a country.

{を契機[けいき]に} means the same but is formal and used in news and business writing, often about social or organisational change.

examples.jp: 留学[りゅうがく]をきっかけに、環境問題[かんきょうもんだい]に興味[きょうみ]を持[も]つようになった。
examples.en: Studying abroad got me interested in environmental issues.

examples.jp: 結婚[けっこん]したのをきっかけに、料理[りょうり]を始[はじ]めた。
examples.en: I started cooking when I got married.

examples.jp: 友人[ゆうじん]の一言[ひとこと]がきっかけで、転職[てんしょく]を考[かんが]え始[はじ]めた。
examples.en: A single remark from a friend made me start thinking about changing jobs.

examples.jp: 今回[こんかい]の事故[じこ]を契機[けいき]に、安全対策[あんぜんたいさく]の見直[みなお]しが進[すす]められている。
examples.en: Prompted by this accident, safety measures are being reviewed.

quiz.q: アニメを見[み]たの＿＿、日本語[にほんご]の勉強[べんきょう]を始[はじ]めた。
quiz.en: Watching anime was what got me started studying Japanese.

quiz.q: 祖母[そぼ]の入院[にゅういん]が＿＿、家族[かぞく]で過[す]ごす時間[じかん]が増[ふ]えた。
quiz.en: Our grandmother's hospital stay led to our family spending more time together.

units.title: Outcomes, completion, and unfinished business
units.summary: How a long process ended ({あげく}, {末[すえ]に}), futile effort ({たところで}), doing without ({ことなく}), finishing completely ({きる}), stopping halfway ({かける}), and leaving things as they are ({っぱなし}).

points.title: 〜あげく（に）
points.meaning: after a lot of ..., in the end (unfortunately)
points.structure: V-た + あげく（に）　／　Noun + の + あげく（に）
points.explanation:
{あげく} describes a long, often troublesome process (worrying, arguing, waiting, getting lost) that ends in a **disappointing or bad result**. The speaker usually sounds frustrated or exasperated.

It often follows expressions of repeated or prolonged action: {さんざん}, {いろいろ}, {何時間[なんじかん]も}, {迷[まよ]いに迷[まよ]った}.

The phrase {あげくの果[は]てに} means "on top of all that, in the end..." and introduces the worst outcome of all.

examples.jp: さんざん迷[まよ]ったあげく、結局[けっきょく]何[なに]も買[か]わなかった。
examples.en: After agonising over it for ages, I ended up buying nothing.

examples.jp: 長時間[ちょうじかん]の議論[ぎろん]のあげく、計画[けいかく]は白紙[はくし]に戻[もど]った。
examples.en: After hours of discussion, the plan went back to square one.

examples.jp: 道[みち]に迷[まよ]ったあげくに、終電[しゅうでん]まで逃[のが]してしまった。
examples.en: After getting lost, I even ended up missing the last train.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は散々[さんざん]文句[もんく]を言[い]ったあげく、会費[かいひ]も払[はら]わずに帰[かえ]ってしまった。
examples.en: After complaining endlessly, he went home without even paying the fee.

points.notes: {あげく} → negative or disappointing result. {末[すえ]に} → neutral or positive result after long effort (next point).

quiz.q: さんざん待[ま]たされた＿＿、面接[めんせつ]は中止[ちゅうし]になった。
quiz.en: After being kept waiting for ages, the interview was cancelled.

quiz.q: 一時間[いちじかん]も店員[てんいん]に文句[もんく]を言[い]った＿＿、その客[きゃく]は何[なに]も買[か]わずに帰[かえ]った。
quiz.en: After complaining to the staff for a whole hour, the customer left without buying anything.

points.title: 〜末[すえ]に / 〜の末[すえ]
points.meaning: after (a long process of); finally
points.structure: V-た + 末[すえ]（に）　／　Noun + の + 末[すえ]（に）
points.explanation:
{末[すえ]} means "end". {〜た末[すえ]に} says that after a long or difficult process (thinking, discussion, research, a hard-fought match) a **result was finally reached**. Unlike {あげく}, the result can be positive or neutral, and the focus is on the effort that led there.

It is somewhat formal and very common in news reports: {延長戦[えんちょうせん]の末[すえ]} ("after extra time"), {協議[きょうぎ]の末[すえ]} ("after deliberation").

{に} is often dropped in writing: {研究[けんきゅう]の末[すえ]、〜}.

examples.jp: 悩[なや]んだ末[すえ]に、日本[にほん]で就職[しゅうしょく]することに決[き]めた。
examples.en: After a lot of soul-searching, I decided to get a job in Japan.

examples.jp: 何度[なんど]も話[はな]し合[あ]った末[すえ]に、ようやく結論[けつろん]が出[で]た。
examples.en: After discussing it many times, we finally reached a conclusion.

examples.jp: 三年間[さんねんかん]の研究[けんきゅう]の末[すえ]、新[あたら]しい薬[くすり]が完成[かんせい]した。
examples.en: After three years of research, the new drug was completed.

examples.jp: 延長戦[えんちょうせん]の末[すえ]、日本代表[にほんだいひょう]が勝利[しょうり]した。
examples.en: Japan's national team won after extra time.

quiz.q: 激[はげ]しい議論[ぎろん]の＿＿、法案[ほうあん]は可決[かけつ]された。
quiz.en: After heated debate, the bill was passed.

quiz.q: 努力[どりょく]を重[かさ]ねた＿＿、ついに夢[ゆめ]だった医者[いしゃ]になった。
quiz.en: After years of hard work, she finally became the doctor she'd dreamed of being.

points.title: 〜たところで
points.meaning: even if (you do); it's no use
points.structure: V-た + ところで
points.explanation:
{たところで} means "even if you do X, (it won't help / the result will be small)". The second half is negative or dismissive: {無駄[むだ]だ}, {どうにもならない}, {間[ま]に合[あ]わない}, or a small amount with {せいぜい} ("at most").

It is often paired with {いくら} or {どんなに}: {いくら謝[あやま]ったところで} ("no matter how much you apologise").

Compared with {〜ても}, it stresses **futility**. Don't confuse it with {ところで} ("by the way") or {〜たところ} ("when I did, it turned out").

examples.jp: 今[いま]から急[いそ]いだところで、もう間[ま]に合[あ]わないだろう。
examples.en: Even if we hurry now, we won't make it.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]に相談[そうだん]したところで、どうにもならない。
examples.en: There's no point in consulting him; it won't change anything.

examples.jp: いくら謝[あやま]ったところで、許[ゆる]してはもらえないだろう。
examples.en: No matter how much I apologise, I doubt I'll be forgiven.

examples.jp: 値上[ねあ]げしたところで、せいぜい百円[ひゃくえん]程度[ていど]だ。
examples.en: Even if they raise the price, it'll be by a hundred yen at most.

quiz.q: 今[いま]さら後悔[こうかい]した＿＿、何[なに]も変[か]わらない。
quiz.en: Even if you regret it now, nothing will change.

quiz.q: 部長[ぶちょう]に頼[たの]んだところで、＿＿。
quiz.en: Even if we ask the manager, he probably won't listen.
choices: 聞[き]いてくれないだろう
きっと聞[き]いてくれる

points.title: 〜ことなく
points.meaning: without (ever) doing
points.structure: V-dictionary + ことなく
points.explanation:
{ことなく} is a formal, written way to say "without doing", equivalent to {〜ずに} / {〜ないで}. It usually describes something that one might expect to happen but that **never** happens: resting, giving up, being noticed, missing a day.

The tone is serious and often admiring, so it suits news, speeches, biographies and company messages: {休[やす]むことなく働[はたら]き続[つづ]けた} ("kept working without a break").

In casual conversation, use {〜ずに} or {〜ないで} instead.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は休[やす]むことなく、十時間[じゅうじかん]働[はたら]き続[つづ]けた。
examples.en: He kept working for ten hours without a break.

examples.jp: 失敗[しっぱい]を恐[おそ]れることなく、挑戦[ちょうせん]してほしい。
examples.en: I want you to take on challenges without fearing failure.

examples.jp: 誰[だれ]にも知[し]られることなく、計画[けいかく]は進[すす]められた。
examples.en: The plan went ahead without anyone finding out.

examples.jp: 二十年間[にじゅうねんかん]、一日[いちにち]も欠[か]かすことなく日記[にっき]を書[か]いている。
examples.en: For twenty years, I've written in my diary without missing a single day.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]は諦[あきら]める＿＿、何度[なんど]も挑戦[ちょうせん]した。
quiz.en: She tried again and again without giving up.

quiz.q: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]も風[かぜ]の日[ひ]も、彼[かれ]は休[やす]む＿＿店[みせ]を開[あ]けた。
quiz.en: Rain or shine, he opened the shop without taking a day off.

points.title: 〜きる / 〜きれない
points.meaning: do completely; (can't) finish all of; utterly
points.structure: V-ます stem + きる / きれる / きれない
points.explanation:
{きる} (from {切[き]る}, "to cut") adds the idea of **finishing all the way**:
- {読[よ]みきる} read to the end, {使[つか]いきる} use up, {走[はし]りきる} run the whole distance
- {きれない}: can't do all of it: {食[た]べきれない} (can't eat it all), {数[かぞ]えきれない} (countless)
- with states, "utterly": {疲[つか]れきる} (exhausted), {困[こま]りきる} (completely at a loss)
- {言[い]い切[き]る}: to declare firmly

The idiom {感謝[かんしゃ]してもしきれない} means "I can never thank you enough".

examples.jp: 一晩[ひとばん]で小説[しょうせつ]を読[よ]みきった。
examples.en: I read the whole novel in one night.

examples.jp: こんなにたくさんの料理[りょうり]、二人[ふたり]では食[た]べきれないよ。
examples.en: The two of us can't possibly eat all this food.

examples.jp: 一日中[いちにちじゅう]働[はたら]いて、疲[つか]れきってしまった。
examples.en: I worked all day and I'm completely exhausted.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]は「必[かなら]ず黒字[くろじ]にする」と言[い]い切[き]った。
examples.en: The president declared firmly, "We will definitely turn a profit."

examples.jp: 皆様[みなさま]には、感謝[かんしゃ]してもしきれません。
examples.en: I can never thank you all enough.

quiz.q: 荷物[にもつ]が多[おお]すぎて、車[くるま]に積[つ]み＿＿。
quiz.en: There's too much luggage; we can't fit it all in the car.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は四十二[よんじゅうに]キロを最後[さいご]まで走[はし]り＿＿。
quiz.en: He ran the full 42 kilometres to the finish.

points.title: 〜かけ / 〜かける
points.meaning: half-done; start to (but not finish); be about to
points.structure: V-ます stem + かける / かけの + Noun / かけだ
points.explanation:
{かける} attached to a verb stem means an action has **started but not finished**: {読[よ]みかけの本[ほん]} (a half-read book), {食[た]べかけのパン} (half-eaten bread), {言[い]いかけてやめた} (started to say something and stopped).

With verbs of sudden change it means "almost, on the verge of": {死[し]にかけた} (nearly died), {忘[わす]れかけていた} (had almost forgotten).

{かけ} behaves as a noun, so it takes {の} before another noun. Be careful: {話[はな]しかける} ("to speak to someone") and {呼[よ]びかける} ("to call out to") are separate fixed verbs with a different meaning.

examples.jp: 読[よ]みかけの本[ほん]が机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に置[お]いてある。
examples.en: There's a half-read book on the desk.

examples.jp: 食[た]べかけのパンを捨[す]てないでください。
examples.en: Please don't throw away the half-eaten bread.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は何[なに]か言[い]いかけて、やめた。
examples.en: He started to say something, then stopped.

examples.jp: 書[か]きかけのメールが保存[ほぞん]されたままになっている。
examples.en: A half-written email is still sitting in my drafts.

examples.jp: 忘[わす]れかけていた夢[ゆめ]を、もう一度[いちど]追[お]いかけてみたい。
examples.en: I want to chase the dream I'd almost forgotten one more time.

quiz.q: テーブルの上[うえ]に、飲[の]み＿＿のコーヒーが残[のこ]っていた。
quiz.en: A half-drunk coffee was left on the table.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]は何[なに]か言[い]い＿＿、口[くち]を閉[と]じた。
quiz.en: She started to say something, then closed her mouth.

points.title: 〜っぱなし
points.meaning: leave (as is); keep on (without a break)
points.structure: V-ます stem + っぱなし（だ / で / にする / の + Noun）
points.explanation:
{っぱなし} (from {放[はな]す}, "to let go") has two uses, both slightly negative:

**1. Leaving something in a state** that should have been dealt with: {電気[でんき]をつけっぱなし} (left the light on), {水[みず]を出[だ]しっぱなし} (left the water running), {開[あ]けっぱなし} (left open).

**2. A state continuing without a break**: {立[た]ちっぱなし} (standing the whole time), {負[ま]けっぱなし} (losing every time).

Compared with {〜たまま}, which is neutral, {っぱなし} suggests carelessness or an unpleasant situation. It is common in everyday speech.

examples.jp: エアコンをつけっぱなしで出[で]かけてしまった。
examples.en: I went out and left the air conditioner on.

examples.jp: 水[みず]を出[だ]しっぱなしにしないでください。
examples.en: Please don't leave the water running.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は一日中[いちにちじゅう]立[た]ちっぱなしで、足[あし]が痛[いた]い。
examples.en: I was on my feet all day today and my legs hurt.

examples.jp: 最近[さいきん]、うちのチームは負[ま]けっぱなしだ。
examples.en: Our team has been losing non-stop recently.

quiz.q: 窓[まど]を開[あ]け＿＿にして寝[ね]たら、風邪[かぜ]をひいた。
quiz.en: I slept with the window left open and caught a cold.

quiz.q: 朝[あさ]から会議[かいぎ]が続[つづ]いて、ずっと座[すわ]り＿＿だった。
quiz.en: Meetings ran back to back from the morning, so I was sitting the whole time.

units.title: Change, correlation, and matching
units.summary: Describing change that goes along with other change ({につれて}, {にしたがって}, {に伴[ともな]って}), change in progress ({つつある}, {一方[いっぽう]だ}), doing two things at once ({つつ}), and adjusting to circumstances ({に応[おう]じて}).

points.title: 〜につれて（につれ）
points.meaning: as (one thing changes, another changes too)
points.structure: Noun / V-dictionary + につれて・につれ
points.explanation:
{につれて} links two **gradual changes**: as X changes, Y changes along with it. Both halves describe change, often with verbs like {〜ていく}, {〜てくる}, {〜くなる}, {増[ふ]える}, {変[か]わる}.

The first half is a change verb ({年[とし]をとる}, {近[ちか]づく}, {上達[じょうたつ]する}) or a noun of change ({時代[じだい]の変化[へんか]}, {経済[けいざい]の発展[はってん]}).

The second half is a natural development, so it is **not** used with the speaker's will, requests or commands. ✗ {年[とし]をとるにつれて、運動[うんどう]しなさい}.

examples.jp: 台風[たいふう]が近[ちか]づくにつれて、風[かぜ]が強[つよ]くなってきた。
examples.en: As the typhoon approached, the wind grew stronger.

examples.jp: 年[とし]をとるにつれて、涙[なみだ]もろくなった。
examples.en: As I've got older, I've become more easily moved to tears.

examples.jp: 時間[じかん]がたつにつれて、町[まち]の様子[ようす]も変[か]わっていった。
examples.en: As time went by, the town changed too.

examples.jp: 日本語[にほんご]が上達[じょうたつ]するにつれて、日本[にほん]での生活[せいかつ]が楽[たの]しくなってきた。
examples.en: As my Japanese improved, life in Japan became more enjoyable.

quiz.q: 夜[よる]が更[ふ]ける＿＿、気温[きおん]が下[さ]がってきた。
quiz.en: As the night wore on, the temperature dropped.

quiz.q: 経済[けいざい]の発展[はってん]＿＿、人々[ひとびと]の生活[せいかつ]も豊[ゆた]かになった。
quiz.en: As the economy developed, people's lives became more prosperous.

points.title: 〜にしたがって（に従[したが]って）
points.meaning: as ...; in accordance with, following
points.structure: Noun / V-dictionary + に従[したが]って・に従[したが]い
points.explanation:
{に従[したが]って} has two meanings.

**1. "As X changes, Y changes"**: nearly the same as {につれて}: {山[やま]を登[のぼ]るに従[したが]って、空気[くうき]が薄[うす]くなる}.

**2. "In accordance with, following"** a rule, instruction, sign or plan: {指示[しじ]に従[したが]ってください}. {につれて} has **no** such meaning, so ✗ {指示[しじ]につれて}.

Also, because meaning 2 involves deliberately following something, {に従[したが]って} can take requests and intentions in the second half. {に従[したが]い} is the formal written form used in notices.

examples.jp: 山[やま]を登[のぼ]るに従[したが]って、空気[くうき]が薄[うす]くなる。
examples.en: The higher you climb the mountain, the thinner the air gets.

examples.jp: 係員[かかりいん]の指示[しじ]に従[したが]って、避難[ひなん]してください。
examples.en: Please evacuate following the staff's instructions.

examples.jp: 矢印[やじるし]に従[したが]って進[すす]んでください。
examples.en: Please proceed following the arrows.

examples.jp: 法律[ほうりつ]に従[したが]い、個人情報[こじんじょうほう]は適切[てきせつ]に管理[かんり]いたします。
examples.en: In accordance with the law, we will manage personal information appropriately.

points.notes: Change + change: {につれて} or {にしたがって}. Following a rule or instruction: only {にしたがって}.

quiz.q: 先生[せんせい]の指示[しじ]＿＿、実験[じっけん]を進[すす]めてください。
quiz.en: Please carry out the experiment following your teacher's instructions.

quiz.q: 学年[がくねん]が上[あ]がる＿＿、授業[じゅぎょう]の内容[ないよう]も難[むずか]しくなる。
quiz.en: As students move up a year, the lessons get harder too.

points.title: 〜に伴[ともな]って（に伴[ともな]い）
points.meaning: along with; as a result of; accompanying
points.structure: Noun / V-dictionary + こと + に伴[ともな]って・に伴[ともな]い　／　Noun + に伴[ともな]う + Noun
points.explanation:
{に伴[ともな]って} says that one change brings another with it. It is **formal** and appears constantly in news, official notices and business documents.

Unlike {につれて}, it does not require gradual, proportional change. It is also used when a single event causes a change: {本社[ほんしゃ]の移転[いてん]に伴[ともな]い、電話番号[でんわばんごう]が変[か]わります} ("with the head office relocation, the phone number will change").

{に伴[ともな]う} + noun is common in headlines: {台風[たいふう]に伴[ともな]う大雨[おおあめ]} ("heavy rain associated with the typhoon").

examples.jp: 人口[じんこう]の減少[げんしょう]に伴[ともな]って、空[あ]き家[や]が増[ふ]えている。
examples.en: With the decline in population, vacant houses are increasing.

examples.jp: 本社[ほんしゃ]の移転[いてん]に伴[ともな]い、電話番号[でんわばんごう]が変更[へんこう]になります。
examples.en: Due to the relocation of our head office, our phone number will change.

examples.jp: 気温[きおん]の上昇[じょうしょう]に伴[ともな]って、熱中症[ねっちゅうしょう]で運[はこ]ばれる人[ひと]が増[ふ]えている。
examples.en: As temperatures rise, more people are being taken to hospital with heatstroke.

examples.jp: 円安[えんやす]に伴[ともな]い、輸入品[ゆにゅうひん]の価格[かかく]が上[あ]がった。
examples.en: With the weaker yen, the prices of imported goods have gone up.

quiz.q: システムの変更[へんこう]＿＿、一時的[いちじてき]にサービスを停止[ていし]いたします。
quiz.en: Due to a system change, we will temporarily suspend the service.

quiz.q: 少子化[しょうしか]に＿＿、廃校[はいこう]になる学校[がっこう]が増[ふ]えている。
quiz.en: With the falling birth rate, more and more schools are closing.

points.title: 〜つつある
points.meaning: be in the process of; be gradually (changing)
points.structure: V-ます stem + つつある
points.explanation:
{つつある} describes a change that is **currently in progress** and moving in one direction: recovering, spreading, disappearing, approaching. It is a formal, written expression found in news, reports and essays.

It is clearer than {〜ている}, which can mean either "in progress" or "already completed": {景気[けいき]は回復[かいふく]している} could mean it has recovered, while {回復[かいふく]しつつある} means it is still on the way.

Use it only with verbs of change. ✗ {ご飯[はん]を食[た]べつつある}.

examples.jp: 景気[けいき]は回復[かいふく]しつつある。
examples.en: The economy is gradually recovering.

examples.jp: 地球[ちきゅう]の気温[きおん]は年々[ねんねん]上昇[じょうしょう]しつつある。
examples.en: Global temperatures are rising year by year.

examples.jp: この地域[ちいき]の伝統[でんとう]は失[うしな]われつつある。
examples.en: This region's traditions are slowly being lost.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]でもキャッシュレス決済[けっさい]が広[ひろ]がりつつある。
examples.en: Cashless payment is spreading in Japan too.

quiz.q: 台風[たいふう]は今[いま]、日本列島[にほんれっとう]に近[ちか]づき＿＿。
quiz.en: The typhoon is now approaching the Japanese archipelago.

quiz.q: 若者[わかもの]の新聞離[しんぶんばな]れが進[すす]み＿＿。
quiz.en: Young people are increasingly moving away from newspapers.

points.title: 〜つつ / 〜つつも
points.meaning: while (doing); although, even while
points.structure: V-ます stem + つつ / つつも
points.explanation:
{つつ} is a formal equivalent of {ながら}, with two uses.

**1. Simultaneous actions** (same subject): {景色[けしき]を楽[たの]しみつつ歩[ある]いた} ("walked while enjoying the scenery"). In business it is common in phrases like {ご意見[いけん]を伺[うかが]いつつ進[すす]めます} ("we will proceed while hearing your views").

**2. Contradiction, "although"** (usually {つつも}): the speaker knows or thinks one thing but does another. Typical verbs: {知[し]りつつ}, {思[おも]いつつ}, {わかっていつつ}. This use often expresses regret or a guilty conscience.

In casual speech, {ながら} / {ながらも} or {のに} would be more natural.

examples.jp: 景色[けしき]を楽[たの]しみつつ、ゆっくり山道[やまみち]を歩[ある]いた。
examples.en: I walked slowly along the mountain path, enjoying the scenery.

examples.jp: 体[からだ]に悪[わる]いと知[し]りつつ、タバコをやめられない。
examples.en: Even though I know it's bad for me, I can't quit smoking.

examples.jp: 早[はや]く返事[へんじ]をしなければと思[おも]いつつも、つい遅[おそ]くなってしまった。
examples.en: Although I kept thinking I had to reply soon, I ended up replying late.

examples.jp: 地域[ちいき]の皆様[みなさま]のご意見[いけん]を伺[うかが]いつつ、計画[けいかく]を進[すす]めてまいります。
examples.en: We will move the plan forward while listening to the views of local residents.

points.notes: Don't confuse {つつ} (while / although) with {つつある} (in the process of changing).

quiz.q: いけないと思[おも]い＿＿、また夜中[よなか]にラーメンを食[た]べてしまった。
quiz.en: Even though I knew I shouldn't, I ate ramen in the middle of the night again.

quiz.q: 両国[りょうこく]は協力[きょうりょく]し＿＿、問題[もんだい]の解決[かいけつ]を目指[めざ]している。
quiz.en: The two countries are aiming to solve the problem while cooperating with each other.

points.title: 〜一方[いっぽう]だ
points.meaning: keep on (getting more / worse); only increasingly
points.structure: V-dictionary + 一方[いっぽう]だ
points.explanation:
{一方[いっぽう]} literally means "one direction". {〜一方[いっぽう]だ} says a trend **keeps going in one direction** with no sign of stopping. It is mostly used for worrying trends: rising prices, worsening illness, increasing workload.

The verb is a change verb in the dictionary form: {増[ふ]える}, {減[へ]る}, {悪[わる]くなる}, {上[あ]がる}, {進[すす]む}.

Don't confuse it with {一方[いっぽう]（で）} meaning "on the other hand / while": {都会[とかい]は便利[べんり]な一方[いっぽう]、家賃[やちん]が高[たか]い}.

examples.jp: 物価[ぶっか]は上[あ]がる一方[いっぽう]だ。
examples.en: Prices just keep going up.

examples.jp: 父[ちち]の病状[びょうじょう]は悪[わる]くなる一方[いっぽう]だった。
examples.en: My father's condition only kept getting worse.

examples.jp: 大都市[だいとし]の人口[じんこう]は増[ふ]える一方[いっぽう]で、地方[ちほう]は減[へ]り続[つづ]けている。
examples.en: The population of big cities keeps growing, while rural areas keep shrinking.

examples.jp: 円安[えんやす]が進[すす]み、海外旅行[かいがいりょこう]の費用[ひよう]は高[たか]くなる一方[いっぽう]だ。
examples.en: With the weakening yen, overseas travel just keeps getting more expensive.

quiz.q: 新[あたら]しい駅[えき]ができてから、この町[まち]の人口[じんこう]は増[ふ]える＿＿だ。
quiz.en: Since the new station opened, this town's population has kept growing.

quiz.q: 雨[あめ]は強[つよ]くなる＿＿で、なかなか止[や]みそうにない。
quiz.en: The rain just keeps getting heavier and doesn't look like it'll stop any time soon.

points.title: 〜に応[おう]じて
points.meaning: according to; depending on; in response to
points.structure: Noun + に応[おう]じて・に応[おう]じ　／　Noun + に応[おう]じた + Noun
points.explanation:
{応[おう]じる} means "to respond, to match". {Xに応[おう]じて} says something is **adjusted to fit X**: budget, age, ability, season, demand, a customer's request. Whatever X turns out to be, Y changes to match it.

It is common in business, services and official explanations: {ご予算[よさん]に応[おう]じて} ("to suit your budget"), {売上[うりあげ]に応[おう]じて} ("in line with sales").

{に応[おう]じた} + noun is used to modify a noun: {レベルに応[おう]じた練習[れんしゅう]} ("practice suited to your level").

examples.jp: ご予算[よさん]に応[おう]じて、プランをお選[えら]びいただけます。
examples.en: You can choose a plan to suit your budget.

examples.jp: 年齢[ねんれい]や体力[たいりょく]に応[おう]じて、運動[うんどう]の量[りょう]を調整[ちょうせい]しましょう。
examples.en: Let's adjust the amount of exercise according to your age and fitness.

examples.jp: 売上[うりあげ]に応[おう]じてボーナスが支給[しきゅう]される。
examples.en: Bonuses are paid in line with sales.

examples.jp: 季節[きせつ]に応[おう]じた服装[ふくそう]を選[えら]ぶことが大切[たいせつ]だ。
examples.en: It's important to choose clothing suited to the season.

points.notes: Compare {に沿[そ]って} (in line with a plan or policy, Unit 10) and {次第[しだい]で} ("depending on", Unit 13).

quiz.q: 給料[きゅうりょう]は、経験[けいけん]や能力[のうりょく]に＿＿決[き]めます。
quiz.en: Salary is set according to experience and ability.

quiz.q: 参加者[さんかしゃ]の人数[にんずう]＿＿、会場[かいじょう]の広[ひろ]さを決[き]めます。
quiz.en: We'll decide on the size of the venue according to the number of participants.

units.title: Setting, range, and limits
units.summary: Formal ways to mark where and across what something happens ({において}, {にわたって}, {を通[つう]じて}), conditions and limits ({限[かぎ]り}, {限[かぎ]りでは}, {に限[かぎ]って}), and leading examples ({をはじめ}).

points.title: 〜において / 〜における
points.meaning: in; at; in the field of (formal)
points.structure: Noun + において（は / も）　／　Noun + における + Noun
points.explanation:
{において} is the formal written equivalent of the location/time particle {で}. It marks the **place, time, situation or field** where something happens: {本社[ほんしゃ]において}, {現代[げんだい]社会[しゃかい]において}, {医療[いりょう]の分野[ぶんや]において}.

You will find it in official announcements, news, academic writing and speeches. In daily conversation, {で} is normal.

To modify a noun, use {における}: {日本[にほん]における外国人[がいこくじん]労働者[ろうどうしゃ]} ("foreign workers in Japan"). Note that {において} cannot directly modify a noun.

examples.jp: 会議[かいぎ]は本社[ほんしゃ]の大会議室[だいかいぎしつ]において行[おこな]われる。
examples.en: The meeting will be held in the main conference room at head office.

examples.jp: 現代[げんだい]社会[しゃかい]において、インターネットは欠[か]かせないものだ。
examples.en: In modern society, the internet is indispensable.

examples.jp: 医療[いりょう]の分野[ぶんや]において、AIの活用[かつよう]が進[すす]んでいる。
examples.en: In the field of medicine, the use of AI is advancing.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]における外国人[がいこくじん]労働者[ろうどうしゃ]の数[かず]は、年々[ねんねん]増[ふ]えている。
examples.en: The number of foreign workers in Japan is increasing year by year.

points.notes: {にとって} ("for, from the standpoint of") and {について} ("about") are different; {において} is purely about setting.

quiz.q: 卒業式[そつぎょうしき]は、大学[だいがく]の講堂[こうどう]＿＿行[おこな]われます。
quiz.en: The graduation ceremony will be held in the university auditorium.

quiz.q: 経済[けいざい]の分野[ぶんや]＿＿協力[きょうりょく]について、両国[りょうこく]の首脳[しゅのう]が話[はな]し合[あ]った。
quiz.en: The leaders of the two countries discussed cooperation in the economic field.

points.title: 〜にわたって（にわたり / にわたる）
points.meaning: over; throughout; spanning (a long time or wide area)
points.structure: Noun (period / range / number of times) + にわたって・にわたり　／　にわたる + Noun
points.explanation:
{にわたって} emphasises that something covers a **long period or a wide range**: {三日間[みっかかん]にわたって} (over three days), {広[ひろ]い範囲[はんい]にわたって} (over a wide area), {十年[じゅうねん]にわたり} (for ten years), {五回[ごかい]にわたって} (in five sessions).

It is formal and typical in news, reports and business. {にわたる} + noun modifies a noun; the set phrase {多岐[たき]にわたる} means "wide-ranging".

Compare {AからBにかけて}, which needs a start and an end point: {関東[かんとう]から東北[とうほく]にかけて}. {にわたって} takes a single noun that already expresses the whole span.

examples.jp: 会議[かいぎ]は三日間[みっかかん]にわたって行[おこな]われた。
examples.en: The conference was held over three days.

examples.jp: 大雨[おおあめ]の影響[えいきょう]で、広[ひろ]い範囲[はんい]にわたって停電[ていでん]が発生[はっせい]した。
examples.en: Due to heavy rain, power outages occurred over a wide area.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は十年[じゅうねん]にわたり、この地域[ちいき]の調査[ちょうさ]を続[つづ]けてきた。
examples.en: He has continued his research in this region for ten years.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]の仕事[しごと]の内容[ないよう]は多岐[たき]にわたる。
examples.en: Her work covers a wide range of tasks.

quiz.q: 工事[こうじ]は二年[にねん]＿＿続[つづ]く予定[よてい]だ。
quiz.en: The construction is scheduled to continue for two years.

quiz.q: 関東地方[かんとうちほう]の広[ひろ]い範囲[はんい]＿＿、雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]り続[つづ]いた。
quiz.en: Snow continued to fall across a wide area of the Kanto region.

points.title: 〜を通[つう]じて / 〜を通[とお]して
points.meaning: through (a means or person); throughout (a period)
points.structure: Noun + を通[つう]じて / を通[とお]して
points.explanation:
Both forms have two meanings.

**1. Means or channel**: "through, via" a person, medium or experience: {友人[ゆうじん]を通[つう]じて知[し]り合[あ]った} (met through a friend), {ボランティアを通[とお]して学[まな]んだ} (learned through volunteering).

**2. Throughout a period**: {一年[いちねん]を通[つう]じて} (all year round), {生涯[しょうがい]を通[つう]じて} (throughout one's life).

The two are largely interchangeable. {通[つう]じて} sounds a bit more formal and neutral (news: information spread via the internet), while {通[とお]して} slightly emphasises a means someone actively uses ({通訳[つうやく]を通[とお]して話[はな]す}, {経験[けいけん]を通[とお]して}).

examples.jp: 友人[ゆうじん]を通[つう]じて、今[いま]の会社[かいしゃ]を紹介[しょうかい]してもらった。
examples.en: I was introduced to my current company through a friend.

examples.jp: この島[しま]は一年[いちねん]を通[つう]じて暖[あたた]かい。
examples.en: This island is warm all year round.

examples.jp: ボランティア活動[かつどう]を通[とお]して、多[おお]くのことを学[まな]んだ。
examples.en: I learned a great deal through volunteer work.

examples.jp: 事故[じこ]の情報[じょうほう]は、テレビやインターネットを通[つう]じて広[ひろ]がった。
examples.en: News of the accident spread through TV and the internet.

quiz.q: 沖縄[おきなわ]は一年[いちねん]＿＿、気候[きこう]が温暖[おんだん]だ。
quiz.en: Okinawa has a mild climate all year round.

quiz.q: テレビの画面[がめん]を＿＿、世界中[せかいじゅう]の人々[ひとびと]がその瞬間[しゅんかん]を見守[みまも]った。
quiz.en: People all over the world watched that moment through their TV screens.

points.title: 〜限[かぎ]り
points.meaning: as long as; unless (ない限り); to the limit of
points.structure: V-dictionary / V-ている / V-ない / Noun + である + 限[かぎ]り　／　できる限[かぎ]り
points.explanation:
{限[かぎ]り} means "limit" and has two main uses.

**1. Condition, "as long as"**: the second half holds true while the condition lasts: {生[い]きている限[かぎ]り} (as long as I live). With a negative, {〜ない限[かぎ]り} means **"unless"**: {雨[あめ]が降[ふ]らない限[かぎ]り、試合[しあい]は行[おこな]う} (unless it rains, the match goes ahead).
